note: Window agent p1200-p1299, 1 Nov 2026. Five corrections: the Ilkhanate's Anatolia and Mesopotamia and the Jochid ulus's Volga-Bashkir lands, left with the nominal Mongol Empire after the 1260 split (events/0, 1, 4); Novgorod's tribute dated to 1259 and not 1241 (events/2, 3); the stray Jin land of 1231-1232 in Gansu and Ningxia (keyframe_overrides/0, 1); the House of Ascania's region, which never resolved for want of the place 'Lauenburg' (keyframe_overrides/2, 3). No rulings.

region.text: Anatolia, the Jazira, Mesopotamia and Iraq and the Armenian Highlands: only the cells the Mongol Empire still holds there pass to Hulegu's ulus (Syria west of the Jazira left out: the Mamluks took it after Ain Jalut in 1260)

events.note: 1261: after the 1259 division the Ilkhanate is an 'Independent khanate (1260-1335)' (infobox), and its lands were Hulegu's, not the Great Khan's: 'the Mongols under Baiju occupied Anatolia, while the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum and the Empire of Trebizond became vassals of the Mongols'; 'The Mongols administered Iraq, the Caucasus, and western and southern Iran directly'. The ulus-of-hulegu_1260 keyframe is drawn without Anatolia and Rum's keyframe shrinks to Kayseri-Aksaray, so about 1,550 Anatolian cells, 500 of the Jazira and 650 of Mesopotamia stayed with the nominal Mongol Empire (draft 1270) until the Ilkhanate's own row in 1294. Dated 1261 so that the 1260 keyframe check has already run. Reviewer, 1 Nov 2026: the leaf {"country": "Syria"} removed here and in events/4. It handed 164 cells of inner Syria (Homs-Palmyra, 36-40E) to the Ilkhanate for 1261-1271, but the page has Hulegu only 'briefly conquering Ayyubid Syria and Aleppo in 1260', the force he left 'defeated at the Battle of Ain Jalut by the Mamluks of Egypt', and the Ilkhanids 'never able to gain and keep significant ground against the Mamluks'; the Battle of Ain Jalut page has the Mamluks take Damascus five days after 3 September 1260 and Aleppo within a month. The Syrian cells inside the Jazira and Mesopotamia regions still pass.

region.text: the Volga region, Bashkiria and Volga Bulgaria: only the cells the Mongol Empire still holds there pass to the Jochid ulus

events.note: 1271: the Jochid ulus became 'a functionally independent khanate' after the division of 1259, and Batu had taken 'the Bashkirs' land and then moving on to Volga Bulgaria in 1236'; the ulus-of-jochi_1267 keyframe (Cliopatria's Golden Horde of 1294) leaves Bashkortostan and the Nizhny Novgorod Volga out and the nominal Mongol Empire picks them up in 1270 (about 450 cells until 1293). Dated 1271 so that the 1267 keyframe check and the Mongol Empire's 1270 keyframe check (which picks the unclaimed cells up again) have already run.

region.text: Novgorod and Pskov land, drawn from the 1285 shapes of the two republics

events.note: 1241: ends the tributary tint the dossier bridged from the Cliopatria gap; Novgorod was not paying tribute yet. 'In 1259, he [Alexander Nevsky] led an army to the city of Novgorod and forced it to pay tribute it had previously refused to the Golden Horde'; the Golden Horde page: 'The Novgorod region in the far northwest was not counted until the winter of 1258-1259'. Replaced by events/3 from 1259.

region.text: Novgorod and Pskov land, drawn from the 1285 shapes of the two republics

events.note: 1259: Novgorod pays tribute to the Golden Horde. 'In 1259, he [Alexander Nevsky] led an army to the city of Novgorod and forced it to pay tribute it had previously refused to the Golden Horde'; the Mongols 'began to ride through the streets, writing down the Christian houses' (the census of 1258-1259). The relation closes when the ulus ends in 1293, as the dossier's own relation did.

region.text: Anatolia, the Jazira, Mesopotamia and Iraq and the Armenian Highlands: only the cells the Mongol Empire still holds there pass to Hulegu's ulus (Syria west of the Jazira left out: the Mamluks took it after Ain Jalut in 1260)

events.note: 1262: second pass of events/0 (redated by the reviewer from 1271). The Mongol Empire's keyframe check of 1261 (mongol-empire_1261, which runs after events/0) takes about 530 cells again: 400 of the Zengid land of Mosul and 130 nobody held, in Iraq, the Jazira and south-east Anatolia; this event hands them to Hulegu's ulus from 1262. The trial shows no later Mongol keyframe (1270, 1279) takes them back, so they no longer stay with the nominal empire 1261-1270 as in the 1271 version. Same page and sentences as events/0: 'The Mongols administered Iraq, the Caucasus, and western and southern Iran directly'; infobox 'Independent khanate (1260-1335)'.

correction.text: Henan and the Huai strip only: the 1216 shape without Hebei, Shanxi, Shandong, Shaanxi and also without Gansu, Ningxia and Inner Mongolia

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's own text for 1231-1232 is 'Henan only', but the 1216 shape it subtracts from also covers east Gansu, Ningxia and Inner Mongolia, so about 470 cells there stayed Jin until 1234 (blue patches beside the Western Xia land in the 1233 render). After Fengxiang fell in 1231 'the Chang'an garrison abandoned the city, pulling back to Henan Province with all the city's population' and the court's last bases were Kaifeng and Caizhou; Gansu is not mentioned by the page.

correction.text: superseded 1227-1230 by the 1223 keyframe and from 1231 by the 1231 and 1233 keyframes

keyframe_overrides.why: Companion of keyframe_overrides/0. The dossier marks this Cliopatria shape 'wrong' and says it is 'valid in no year' because the 1223, 1231 and 1233 keyframes cover 1223-1234, but its years still run 1227-1235 in data/shapes.csv and its correction (the 1216 shape without Hebei, Shanxi and Shandong) is unioned into every keyframe check, so from 1231 it keeps Shaanxi, Gansu, Ningxia and the Huai strip Jin and the 1231 and 1233 keyframes cannot trim them (the 1233 check removes 0 cells). The years are cut to 1227-1230, where the 1223 keyframe has the same shape; the Mongols 'finally took Fengxiang' in 1231 and the garrison pulled back to Henan.

correction.text: Anhalt (Bernburg, Kothen, Dessau and the Aschersleben line), Saxe-Wittenberg with Lauenburg as the undivided Duchy of Saxony of John I and Albert II, and the counts of Weimar-Orlamunde (Lauenburg is given as the region 'Duchy of Saxe-Lauenburg' because the gazetteer has no place 'Lauenburg')

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's own region, with one repair: its {"place": "Lauenburg", "km": 15} does not resolve (the gazetteer has no such place), so the whole union failed and the House of Ascania, born in 1260, owned no land at all from 1260 to 1306. The page: John I and Albert II 'ruled jointly from 1260' over the Duchy of Saxony (Wittenberg and Lauenburg), and the partition into the Lauenburg and Wittenberg lines came only in 1296; Anhalt's Ascanian lines (Bernburg, Aschersleben, Kothen) date from the land division of 1252. The dossier's later keyframes (1307 to 1482) carry the same {"place": "Lauenburg"} element and need the same repair (dossier request).
